items.title: 68087_Cliff Leeman oral history interview
items.q: Louie Belson left the band, Louie had followed Buddy Rich... Tom had been having -- had a fight with Louie Belson.

ctx.x: Well, we tried a couple of times, and the tapes kind of fouled up, and Yank said, 'Let me hear that first one'. And we played back the first tape, and that's the one they took. Now this is a phenomenon in reading something down and have it swing, and the jazz solo, of course, is another thing, too, but everything was just a beautiful, swinging feeling, and so they took the first tape. And I just mention this as an -- such an unusual organization in its field.

Bob Haggart told me to play any way you want to, if it's too loud, we'll call it down in the control room, do whatever you want, just use your own feeling and your own taste -- then he told me what to do. Now, it's seldom in this world, unless you're the leader and you're the drummer, like Buddy Rich -- and there are only one or two of those around, possibly Louie Belson, that anybody that has the opportunity to work with their own natural feeling without somebody standing over them with a baseball bat.
I can still Yank Lawson's voice saying; 'be happy, Cliff, do whatever you want.'1)
